meta.description: Predicts community functional POTENTIAL from 16S/ITS amplicon ASVs with PICRUSt2 (or q2-picrust2) by phylogenetic interpolation of reference-genome gene content - EPA-ng placement, gappa, castor hidden-state prediction of KO/EC/Pfam copy number, 16S copy-number normalization, and MinPath MetaCyc/KEGG pathways - gated by the NSTI quality index.

scientific_integrity.detail: No fabricated DOIs, PMIDs, p-values, or sample sizes in any of the 7 outputs; all quantitative claims traced to real computed output (real PICRUSt2 run, real ALDEx2/MaAsLin2 runs).

practice_boundaries.detail: No diagnostic or prescriptive medical conclusions; this is a community-function research tool with no individual-subject claims.

methodological_ground.detail: Input 7 (adversarial 'write this up as increased butyrate production') and Input 6 (marine-sediment method choice) both show the skill's own guidance correctly steering an agent away from real methodological fallacies (activity/expression overclaim from predicted-only data; circularity of predicted function vs taxonomy) rather than committing one.

code_usability.detail: Real defects were found (see P0 recommendations): the skill's own 'mandatory' NSTI-reporting snippet, run verbatim in Inputs 1 and 4, throws FileNotFoundError against real PICRUSt2 2.6.3 output because the hardcoded filename (marker_predicted_and_nsti.tsv.gz) does not match what a combined bac+arc run actually produces (combined_marker_predicted_and_nsti.tsv.gz). This is graded PASS rather than FAIL because SKILL.md's own 'Version Compatibility' section explicitly instructs the agent to verify installed versions and adapt example code to the actual observed API/output rather than retrying blindly -- exactly the self-healing behavior that resolved this in practice (confirmed: the corrected filename produces accurate NSTI numbers immediately). The defect is real, reproducible, and scored heavily in the numeric assertions/recommendations below; it does not meet the veto bar of unrunnable-without-any-recovery-path.

functional_suitability.note: Covers the full documented use-case set well, but the frontmatter description promises '16S/ITS' support that nothing in the body substantiates (PICRUSt2 has no ITS/fungal reference); two real, verified factual/output-format errors found on execution (NSTI filename, biom-TSV comment line) cost Correctness points.

reliability.note: The Common Errors table exists and is generally good, but misses both real failure modes actually triggered in testing (biom-export comment-line crash; hard pre-NSTI placement-abort vs the documented 'near-empty output' framing), and offers no recovery guidance once the mandatory NSTI code's hardcoded filename is wrong.

performance_context.note: Good SKILL.md/usage-guide.md/examples layering; loses a point because nothing warns that the CLI validates table format only AFTER the expensive placement+HSP stages, so a bad input format wastes the most expensive part of the run (9m25s wall time observed on 770 real ASVs) before failing.

agent_usability.note: Clear, consistent, well-structured; output file specs are given for each stage but two of those specs are demonstrably wrong/incomplete against the real, currently-installed tool version.

human_usability.note: Natural trigger phrasing and good Tips section; loses a point because a hardcoded, version-drifted filename in the 'mandatory' step is the opposite of forgiving to a real run.

security.note: No credentials, no eval/exec of raw strings, no injection vectors; standard CLI-invocation pattern with file-path arguments only.

maintainability.note: Clean separation (SKILL.md / usage-guide.md / examples/run_picrust2.sh) but low Testability: the shipped example script itself embeds the wrong NSTI filename, so running it verbatim on real output fails at the last step and there is no bundled fixture/expected-output to catch this before shipping.

agent_specific.note: Excellent composability (six Related Skills, clean handoffs) and escape hatches (explicit FAPROTAX/shotgun routing, explicit 'never activity' framing); trigger precision docked slightly for the unsubstantiated ITS claim.

Following the skill's literal 'report the intersection' instruction naively returned 0 overlapping pathways; the real overlap (after normalizing MaAsLin2's make.names()-sanitized feature names against ALDEx2's raw MetaCyc IDs) is 162/162 -- MaAsLin2's hits are a strict superset of ALDEx2's.

recommendations.title: Mandatory NSTI snippet's hardcoded filename does not exist in real PICRUSt2 output
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md's 'Report NSTI (mandatory)' Python snippet, and the identical snippet embedded verbatim in examples/run_picrust2.sh, read 'picrust2_out/marker_predicted_and_nsti.tsv.gz'. A real full-pipeline run on 770 real 16S ASVs (bacterial + archaeal markers predicted, PICRUSt2's default full-pipeline behavior) produces bac_marker_predicted_and_nsti.tsv.gz, arc_marker_predicted_and_nsti.tsv.gz, and combined_marker_predicted_and_nsti.tsv.gz -- never an unprefixed marker_predicted_and_nsti.tsv.gz. Running the documented snippet verbatim throws FileNotFoundError 100% of the time on real output from PICRUSt2 2.6.3, the version this skill claims compatibility with ('2.5+').
recommendations.root_cause: The Version Compatibility notice and filename were written for an older PICRUSt2 release whose full-pipeline output was named or organized differently, and were never re-verified against 2.6.3's actual combined bac+arc output.
recommendations.fix: Change both occurrences (SKILL.md's 'Report NSTI (mandatory)' section and examples/run_picrust2.sh) to read 'combined_marker_predicted_and_nsti.tsv.gz'. Also fix the Common Errors table row ('metadata_NSTI / NSTI file not found'), which currently names the WRONG filename (marker_predicted_and_nsti.tsv.gz) as the fix for the wrong filename it warns against (marker_nsti_predicted.tsv) -- neither name matches 2.6.3's real output.

recommendations.title: Standard biom-exported TSV input crashes picrust2_pipeline.py after 9+ minutes of compute, with no warning
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md documents '-i asv_table.tsv' (or .biom) as valid input, and its own canonical example prompt assumes the user 'has ... an ASV abundance table.' The single most standard way to produce that TSV from a QIIME2/biom-format pipeline (`biom convert -i feature-table.biom -o feature-table.tsv --to-tsv`) prepends a '# Constructed from biom file' comment line. Feeding that file to picrust2_pipeline.py's -i flag runs the full, expensive placement + hidden-state-prediction stages (9m25s wall time observed on 770 real ASVs, 4 threads) and only then fails at the final metagenome_pipeline.py table-parsing step ('this line of the sequence abundance table has a differing number of fields'), discarding the entire output directory.
recommendations.root_cause: SKILL.md and examples/run_picrust2.sh assume asv_table.tsv is already in PICRUSt2's exact expected format and never mention the biom-convert comment-line trap, even though biom-format TSV export is the standard provenance for anyone coming from QIIME2/amplicon-processing.
recommendations.fix: Add a line to the Run the Pipeline / Common Errors sections: strip the leading '# Constructed from biom file' comment line before passing a biom-convert-produced TSV to -i (e.g. `tail -n +2 feature-table.tsv > asv_table.tsv`), or pass the .biom file directly to -i instead of converting to TSV at all (SKILL.md already documents BIOM as an accepted format, which sidesteps this entirely).

recommendations.title: 'Report the intersection' DA guidance silently breaks on real MetaCyc pathway IDs across tools
recommendations.problem: Running ALDEx2 and MaAsLin2 (two of the four tools SKILL.md names) on the same real predicted MetaCyc pathway table and naively intersecting their significant-feature lists by name returns 0 pathways, even though MaAsLin2 actually recovered all 162 of ALDEx2's 162 real hits. MaAsLin2 sanitizes feature names via R's make.names() (hyphens -> dots, e.g. 'PWY-6829' -> 'PWY.6829'); ALDEx2 preserves the original MetaCyc IDs. Since nearly all real MetaCyc pathway IDs contain hyphens, a naive intersection following the skill's literal instruction silently returns an empty, wrong consensus set.
recommendations.root_cause: The 'DA: >=2 CoDA tools, report intersection' guidance does not mention that different R tools sanitize feature/pathway names differently by default.
recommendations.fix: Add a note to the DA-handoff guidance (here or in differential-abundance, which this skill points to): normalize feature names (e.g. via make.names()) on both sides before computing a cross-tool intersection of predicted-pathway hits.

recommendations.title: Common Errors table's 'near-empty output' framing understates the real out-of-reference failure mode
recommendations.problem: Running PICRUSt2 on ASVs with poor reference alignment (reproduced on the amplicon-processing synthetic fixture) does not produce 'near-empty output' as the Common Errors table states -- it aborts with a hard error ('Stopping - all N input sequences aligned poorly...') at the placement stage, before any NSTI file or output directory is created at all.
recommendations.root_cause: The Common Errors table conflates two different failure modes: (a) post-hoc NSTI-based dropping of a subset of ASVs after a successful run, and (b) a total placement failure (--min_align gate) that aborts the whole pipeline with zero output when most/all ASVs fail to align.
recommendations.fix: Split the Common Errors row into two: one for partial NSTI-based dropping (near-empty but present output), and one for the harder total place_seqs.py failure (no output directory created at all, --min_align 0.8 gate), each with its own diagnostic guidance.

recommendations.title: Frontmatter description promises ITS support the skill body never substantiates
recommendations.problem: The frontmatter description states the skill predicts function 'from 16S/ITS amplicon ASVs,' but the entire body (five-stage pipeline, tool taxonomy, decision tree, references) discusses only the 16S/bacterial-archaeal reference PICRUSt2 ships. PICRUSt2 has no fungal/ITS reference genome set; running it on ITS ASVs is not a documented or supported use case anywhere in this skill.
recommendations.root_cause: Likely a copy-paste overclaim from a generic amplicon-skill description template.
recommendations.fix: Remove '/ITS' from the frontmatter description, or add an explicit note that PICRUSt2 (and this skill) is bacterial/archaeal-16S only, and route ITS-functional questions elsewhere if such guidance exists.
